extracted.intended_audience: university faculty researchers and multidisciplinary teams preparing MURI (ARO/ONR/AFOSR) proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and topic-specific requirements for writing FY25 Multidisciplinary University Research Initiative (MURI) proposals across several ARO/ONR/AFOSR topics. Includes objectives, suggested research concentration areas, budget/team constraints, and special participation notes per topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: To develop and explore novel QML approaches to process quantum data, and to enable enhancements over the currently best quantum and classical methods.
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective:  To develop and explore novel QML approaches to process quantum data, and to enable enhancements over the currently best quantum and classical methods. Specifically we envision exploiting quantum sensor data to avoid QRAM complications. This could open the possibility of advancing quantum sensing while also expanding our understanding of the kinds of data structures which are amenable to quantum speed ups and accuracy gains, and perhaps also informing the development of enhanced classical machine learning algorithms and approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (QML with quantum sensor data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Suggested research areas include but are not limited to: (1) fundamental analysis of the types of data best suited for QML, collected from various quantum sensors either in local or distributed configurations; (2) fundamental analysis of and innovations in QML platforms and their optimization for quantum sensing applications; (3) methods for comparing fundamental operations in quantum and classical ML realms and their limitations, to better understand under what circumstances which approach is optimal; and (4) optimal methods of collecting either static or time dependent data amenable for QML processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Emphasizes exploiting quantum sensor data to avoid QRAM complications; goals include understanding data structures amenable to quantum speed-ups, scaling with sensor parameters, and identifying optimal QML algorithms. Anticipated Resources: No more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources (QML topic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Resources: No more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative note: Topic Research Topic Chiefs provided for clarification and discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Elucidate and understand genetic, chemical, and structural mechanisms for structural color in bacteria/fungi and engineer living bio-hybrid systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: The objectives of this MURI are to elucidate and understand the genetic, chemical, and structural mechanisms responsible for naturally occurring structural color in bacteria and/or fungi; to use this understanding to translate naturally occurring structural color pathways and/or create novel engineered structural color systems in bacteria and/or fungi; and to engineer living bio-hybrid systems where inorganic nanomaterials are interfaced with engineered bacteria/fungi to enable external stimuli response and dynamic modulation of structural color on demand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (In Living Color)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Suggested research areas include but are not limited to: (1) Elucidate the genetic and chemical pathways that are responsible for naturally occurring structural color in bacteria and fungi; (2) Characterize and model the relationships between optical properties and 3D structure in these microbes; (3) Explore synthetic biology approaches to translate naturally occurring structural color pathways and/or create novel engineered structural color pathways in bacteria and/or fungi to create engineered living systems displaying structural color at the single-cell and/or collective level; (4) Design, create, and characterize bio-hybrid systems where nanomaterials are interfaced with engineered bacterial and/or fungal cells to provide additional optical functionality and/or sensitivity to external stimuli and explore approaches to dynamically tune these systems in situ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications may translate pathways into model organisms (e.g., E. coli or S. cerevisiae) and interface cells with plasmonic or magnetic nanoparticles to enable stimuli-responsiveness and dynamic modulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources (In Living Color) and HBCU/MI participation note
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Resources: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for up to 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for Topic 10 are invited that include participation from eligible HBCUs/MIs (as defined in Section I. Overview of the Research Opportunity); however, HBCU/MI participation is not a requirement. Applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Discover biological and mathematical control principles for bidirectional LNN-ANN communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: Explore how biology transforms information for data efficient and adaptive learning, by discovering biological and mathematical control principles underlying bidirectional communication between living and non-living neural networks. Outcomes are anticipated to enable hybrid networks with energy- and data-efficient training methods, complex adaptive learning and reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (Large-scale Bi-directional Control for Hybrid Adaptive Networks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Research concentration areas may include but are not limited to the following: 1) understanding and shaping dynamics of LNN information processing (constructed in-vitro cultured networks); 2) exploring and developing LNN architectures based on mathematical and computing principles for communicating between ANNs and LNNs; 3) new protocols and approaches for optimization of data and energy in training methods; 4) ANN-LNN hardware emulation principles for bidirectional prediction and control; and 5) modular extensible ANN-LNN networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context: Emphasizes creating a protocol 'language' true to biological dynamics and customizable LNN architectures; leverage optogenetics, spatial light modulators, and neuromorphic emulators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources (Hybrid Adaptive Networks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Resources: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no larger than $1.5M per year for five years and fund no more than six faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs during the white paper phase of the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Design, create, understand, and dynamically tune piezo-composite metamaterials that display EM coupling
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: This topic seeks a theoretical, computational, and experimental framework with which to design, create, understand, and dynamically tune new piezo-composite metamaterials that display EM coupling and ability to detect and precisely control elastic and acoustic wave propagation using external electric fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (Electro-momentum Coupled Piezoelectric Metamaterials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Suggested research areas include, but are not limited to: 1) Advanced high-dimensional theory of EM coupling and general Willis coupling between elasticity, dynamics and electrostatics; 2) Computational (analytic, simulation and data driven) tools to design piezoelectric metamaterials platforms with composition and structure maximizing EM coupling; 3) Piezo-composite fabrication and processing into metamaterials with complex heterogeneous architectures and multiscale features; 4) Novel techniques to structurally and functionally characterize EM coupled piezo-composites to elucidate underlying mechanisms; 5) Exploration of EM coupling phenomena in acoustic metamaterials for elastic and acoustic wave manipulation via external electric stimulus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motivation: Realizing EM-coupling requires new simulation tools, advanced fabrication, and characterization methodologies; physical manifestations would enable tunable and responsive acoustic devices for sensing and transduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources (Piezoelectric Metamaterials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Resources: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Revolutionize design of polymers whose degradation is actuated by biotoxin recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: This MURI seeks to revolutionize the design and synthesis of a novel class of polymers or polymer assemblies that trigger rapid and selective depolymerization or disassembly via binding of a broad range of naturally occurring biomolecular agents such as toxins present in complex environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (Actuation of Polymeric Degradation via Biotoxin Recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Focus areas may include but are not limited to: (1) Design of monomers, polymers, polymer assemblies and/or polymer-protein conjugates that are stable in harsh environments, non-toxic, and rapidly degrade upon appropriate binding; (2) Computational modeling at and across appropriate spatial/temporal scales to converge on design of recognition elements specific to biotoxin structures and the mechanism of initiation of depolymerization or disassembly; (3) For complex environments, in vitro and/or in vivo analysis of microbial, biochemical and physical features as a function of different conditions to direct the effective design of the polymer chemistry; (4) Structural biology and/or in silico molecular-level structure analysis of biotoxin-polymeric binding complexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeling techniques suggested include molecular dynamics, particle-based simulations, continuum multiscale mechanistic models, and ML/genetic algorithms to optimize designs. Emphasis on stability in complex heterogeneous environments and high selectivity/sensitivity of recognition elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources (Polymeric Degradation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Resources: Up to $1.5M/year for 5 years to support up to six funded faculty members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with the topic chiefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Develop mechanistic understanding of atomic scale defect 'phase' dynamics
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: Develop a mechanistic understanding of atomic scale defect "phase" dynamics to predict how populations of heterogeneities may be manipulated via external forcings to drive mechanical, chemical, and/or thermal behaviors of bulk materials. Electromagnetic, optical, and other functional material properties are not of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (Defect Phase Dynamics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Suggested areas include but are not limited to: (1) identifying key defect populations in model material systems and representing them as population 'networks'; (2) developing theoretical and computational approaches to probe thresholds for manipulating defect phase activity via external mechanical, chemical, and/or thermal loads and validating experimentally; (3) identifying dominant defect phase networks and developing approaches for describing interactions with other defect systems; (4) elucidating defect flux/phase changes across boundaries, surfaces and interfaces to identify how defect (meta)stability may control bulk material behaviors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term outputs may include atomistic to microscopic understanding of defect phases and/or defect phase diagram representations. Note explicit exclusion: electromagnetic, optical, and other functional material properties are not of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources (Defect Phase Dynamics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Resources: No more than an average of $1.5M per year for five years, supporting no more than six funded faculty researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with topic chiefs during the white paper phase of solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Infer path-dependent constitutive models for solid-gas interphases under non-equilibrium conditions using physics-constrained perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: Discover path-dependent constitutive models of solid-gas interphase behaviors under non-equilibrium conditions using physics-constrained perception integrated with relevant experimental observables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (Inferring Solid-Gas Interphase Responses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Potential areas include but are not limited to: (1) Physics-constrained learning approaches incorporating mechanical deformations, chemical reactions, and/or mass loss; (2) Determinations of key history-dependent spatiotemporal information required to bound and bias learning approaches for solid-gas interphases toward physically relevant behaviors (may include 'operando' characterization approaches); (3) Forward predictions across relevant length and time scales, incorporating uncertainty bounds for given solid-gas systems and non-equilibrium conditions to validate inferred models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Near-term outputs may include demonstrating ability to learn behaviors of well-characterized model solid-gas systems to enable inferring more complex behaviors. Emphasis on thermodynamically-consistent models and integration with experimental observables.

Overview of the Research Opportunity); however, HBCU/MI participation is not a requirement. Applications with an HBCU/MI MURI team member may be eligible for $1.5M in total additional funds. Exceptions warranted by specific proposal approaches should be discussed with topic chiefs during the white paper phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective: Use quantum simulators to study materials properties and accelerate materials design
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective: The objective of this MURI is to study materials properties at the microscopic level using quantum simulator platforms and model systems implemented on them to gain new fundamental insights into the mechanical, thermal, and/or vibrational behavior of materials. A secondary objective is to use quantum simulator platforms to accelerate the iterative process of identifying and designing new materials with physical properties of interest. The particular interest here is explorations that take us beyond purely electronic, spintronic, optoelectronic, and photonic behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Concentration Areas (Quantum Simulators for Materials Design)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Concentration Areas: Suggested research areas include but are not limited to: (1) theoretical approaches (computational and analytical) to design real or model materials; (2) experimental quantum simulation techniques and platforms to explore materials properties and behavior; (3) theoretical tools for understanding and extracting the materials properties from quantum simulations; (4) materials fabrication and characterization techniques for benchmarking simulation results and realizing new materials designs; (5) incorporating insights and data from quantum simulators into computational materials science techniques to improve fidelity, functionality, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on going beyond electronic/spintronic/photonic behaviors to examine mechanical, thermal, vibrational, and non-equilibrium properties; benchmarking against traditional experimental and computational methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipated Resources (Quantum Simulators)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipated Resources: It is anticipated that awards under this topic will be no more than an average of $1.5M per year for up to 5 years, supporting no more than 6 funded faculty.
